name: pareto-two-objectives
description: Two-objective MAB with a concave part in its Pareto front (as in Drugan and Nowe, 2013), Gaussian noise 0.2, 20 runs. Regret of the 0.5 / 0.5 scalarization and Pareto measures.

notices.title: Default hyperparameters
notices.text: alpha=1 for ParetoUCB1 and UCB1. These are the values of the papers. They are safe in theory but often explore too much. To tune them, run a grid search: param_grid=True ("param_grid": true in a config file). Or set them yourself, e.g. ParetoUCB1(alpha=0.1).

notices.title: Assumed constants
notices.text: The problem does not give them, so the policies assume b=1 (reward_range, for ParetoUCB1 and UCB1). If you know the true values, pass them to the policies.

notices.title: Not stored
notices.text: Pseudo-regret ("pseudo_regret"), reward per objective ("reward_vec"), per-action estimates ("estimates"), action of every step ("actions"). The charts cannot show them. The brackets say how to store each one: a quoted name goes in track ("track": [...] in a config file).

notices.title: One point every 50 steps
notices.text: Curves keep one point every 50 steps, plus the last step. Between two points, the line is drawn, not measured. You set log_interval=50. log_interval=1 keeps every step (larger files).

notices.title: Slower timings
notices.text: measure_memory=True makes Python code about 5 times slower. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same setting.

notices.title: Parallel runs
notices.text: n_jobs=4: runs in parallel, one BLAS thread each. Compare CPU times only between runs with the same n_jobs.
